title: Grouping / partition
summary: A precise grouping can be modeled as a partition or as a map assigning objects to classes.

context.note: Revision 2 exposes a QEVA foundation dependency instead of stopping only at a textual framework label.

assumptions.text: A set X and a grouping criterion or assignment are specified.

content.plain: Grouping makes some distinctions irrelevant by assigning multiple objects to the same class.
content.exact: A partition P of a set X is a family of nonempty subsets whose union is X and whose distinct members are disjoint. Equivalently, an equivalence relation ~ on X induces classes [x]={y in X:y~x}.
content.example: Integers grouped by parity form the two classes even and odd.
content.caveat: Not every informal act of grouping is best modeled by a partition: overlapping clusters and probabilistic memberships require other structures.

relations.note: Parity is a two-class grouping of integers modulo 2.
